title: Rational positive Tate tensor powers: bounded constructibility and composition
statement: Fix ell, rational coefficients E or the specified algebraic closure, and a positive-characteristic field k of characteristic different from ell [sk-def-sfb-condensed-ring; sk-def-sfb-qlbar-condensed; sk-def-sfb-dc-setting]. Define T(f,d) as ordinary derived inverse image along f followed by derived tensor with the recorded sectionwise degree-d Tate power transported back to internal modules, followed by shift [2d] [sk-def-sp-tate-twist; def-sfb-module-upper-star]. For separated finite-type k-schemes, T(f,d) preserves Dbc [sk-def-sfb-constructible]. For all composable k-morphisms f:X to Y and g:Y to Z, T(g,d) followed by T(f,e) is naturally isomorphic to T(f followed by g,d+e). Degree zero tensor with its shift is naturally the identity; degree one is the original internal-line tensor.

source.place: First paragraph (composition and induction); second paragraph (preservation).

proof.text: The internal/sectionwise module equivalence identifies its tensor unit and tensor product with the recorded sectionwise unit and tensor product. Induction gives an isomorphism from the transported nonnegative signed power to the corresponding internal tensor power. Rank-one local freeness of the Tate line gives exact sectionwise tensor, hence internal flatness. A K-flat single complex comparison identifies the single of the internal tensor power with the corresponding power in the derived monoidal category.

proof.text: Use the existing locallyFree_of_trivial_cover helper from IntegralTateLineConstructible to transport the common sectionwise root-cover trivializations to raw internal inverse image. The lisse_of_raw_free helper from CoefficientHeartLisseRestriction transports these free models to the normalized coefficient pullback. Thus the rational Tate line is lisse and has finite constant local models. Its single complex and the tensor unit are constructible. Rational tensor closure gives all nonnegative derived powers by induction. Exact derived pullback preserves bounded constructibility, and triangulated shift closure supplies the shift. These arguments include the empty scheme and degree zero.

proof.text: Use Cartesian inverse image of the internal Tate line and its single-complex comparison. Strong monoidality identifies inverse image of a tensor power with the power of inverse image. Associate tensor powers and add their nonnegative exponents. Commute exact derived pullback and derived tensor past shifts, compose inverse images by leftDerivedUpperStarComp, and add shifts. Whisker these natural isomorphisms with the transported-power comparisons to obtain the stated functor isomorphism on the unbounded categories. Degree-one and degree-zero identifications are the original equivalence unit and tensor/shift unitors.
